artworks.title: Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: In this Baroque masterpiece (oil on canvas, 206 × 297 cm, Museo del Prado, Madrid), Guido Reni freezes the decisive instant of the famous footrace. The huntress Atalanta, who vowed to wed only the suitor who could outrun her, stoops mid-stride to snatch one of the three golden apples that Hippomenes (Melanion in other versions) has cast to break her pace, while he surges ahead toward victory. Reni stages the contest as a near-abstract ballet of two pale nude bodies pulling in opposite directions across a darkened ground, their swirling drapery and outstretched limbs forming a taut diagonal counterpoint that has made the picture one of the most celebrated images in Italian painting. A near-identical version hangs in the Capodimonte Museum in Naples.

artworks.title: The Race between Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: Painted for the French royal collection and now in the Musée du Louvre, Noël Hallé's grand canvas treats the contest of Atalanta and Hippomenes with the airy elegance of the French Rococo. The two runners stream across a sunlit classical landscape framed by columns and spectators, Atalanta caught in the fatal hesitation as she bends after a scattered golden apple while Hippomenes—aided by Aphrodite, whose gift the apples were—races on. Hallé subordinates the eroticism of earlier treatments to a decorative, theatrical sweep of movement and light, presenting the myth as a courtly allegory of love conquering pride.

artworks.title: Atalanta and Meleager Hunt the Calydonian Boar
artworks.description: This Flemish Baroque collaboration unites the animal-and-hunt specialist Jan Fyt with the figure painter Pieter Thijs to depict the great boar hunt of Calydon. The huntress Atalanta—who in many tellings drew first blood on the monstrous beast sent by the wrathful Artemis—appears among the assembled heroes alongside Meleager, the prince who awarded her the spoils and whose love for her would set off a fatal family quarrel. Fyt's dramatic rendering of the straining hounds and bristling boar lends the canvas a charged naturalism, while Thijs's figures supply the heroic mythological cast at the heart of one of antiquity's most celebrated hunts.

artworks.title: Meleager and Atalanta (wall painting from Pompeii)
artworks.description: Recovered from a house at Pompeii (region VI 9 3) and now in the National Archaeological Museum of Naples, this Roman fresco shows Atalanta seated beside the hero Meleager in the quiet aftermath of the Calydonian boar hunt. The painting belongs to a popular Campanian decorative repertoire in which mythological lovers are posed in intimate repose; Atalanta, conventionally the only woman among the band of hunters, is paired with Meleager as the prince who honored her with the trophy. As a surviving ancient image it offers rare evidence of how the myth was visualized in the Roman world long before its Baroque revival.
